expected_evidence: Geological: a stratigraphically discrete platinum (and other platinum-group-element) enrichment horizon within Greenland ice cores (e.g., GISP2/NEEM) dated to ~12,900 cal BP / -10950, analogous to the real published Pt spike reported by Petaev et al. (2013) at the Younger Dryas onset

Geological/material: coeval terrestrial 'black mat' or dark organic-rich layer at archaeological/paleontological sites across North America and Eurasia containing magnetic microspherules, meltglass, and nanodiamonds synchronous with the ice-core anomaly

Astronomical: orbital-dynamics modeling or meteor-stream data linking the fallout timing to a dense filament of the Taurid meteor/comet complex (debris stream intersecting Earth's orbit around that epoch)
Geological: correlated iridium or other extraterrestrial trace-element anomalies in independent sediment cores (lake, marine) of the same age for cross-validation
Model-prior (low-tier, unverified): analogy to other well-documented impact/airburst events (e.g., Tunguska-style ejecta signatures) used to argue plausibility of the mechanism
Genetic: possible signature of a Younger Dryas megafaunal population bottleneck coincident with the fallout event (weak, indirect line of evidence)
response.rationale: The interval -10950 corresponds closely to the Younger Dryas onset (~12,900 cal BP), so the 'younger-dryas' detectability row is the appropriate reference rather than a broader Upper Paleolithic default. Ice sheets are exceptionally good archives for exactly this kind of evidence: continuous, datable, low-contamination stratigraphy that preserves fine particulate and geochemical fallout signals for tens of thousands of years, which is why the geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7) detectability scores are the highest in the table for this period. This is consistent with actual published findings I recall from training (model-prior, unverified against the evidence corpus given to me): a platinum anomaly at the Younger Dryas boundary has indeed been reported in Greenland ice cores (Petaev et al. 2013), and platinum/iridium and microspherule/nanodiamond signals have been claimed at several terrestrial sites, associated with the broader 'Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis' tying the event to the Taurid meteor/comet complex. However, I must flag that this same body of work is scientifically contested — multiple independent teams (e.g., Surovell et al. 2009; Pigati et al. 2012, from model-prior recall) failed to replicate the nanodiamond/spherule signal at other sites, so 'corroborated' should be read cautiously as 'partially corroborated by some geochemical data, disputed by other researchers' rather than settled fact. Material (0.35), genetic (0.3), and iconographic/oral_tradition/linguistic/textual evidence (≤0.1) are all poorly suited to this period and mechanism — no written records exist, oral traditions this deep in time are essentially undatable and unreliable, and genetic bottleneck signals are too indirect and confounded by other Younger Dryas climate stressors to serve as strong corroboration. Given that the object and place (platinum-anomaly, Greenland-ice-sheet) map onto the two highest-detectability channels (geological, astronomical) for this period, an absence of strong independent corroborating evidence elsewhere is not surprising and should not be read as strong evidence of falsity — a weighted adjustment of ~0.6 reflects that the core evidence type is quite detectable/preservable, while acknowledging real scientific disagreement over interpretation and replication.
